question: A 4-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his parents for a well-child examination. He has been healthy and has met all development milestones. His immunizations are up-to-date. He is at the 97th percentile for height and 50th percentile for weight. His vital signs are within normal limits. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Auscultation of the heart shows a high-frequency, midsystolic click that is best heard at the fifth left intercostal space. Oral examination shows a high-arched palate. He has abnormally long, slender fingers and toes. The patient is asked to clasp the wrist of the opposite hand and the little finger and thumb overlap. Slit lamp examination shows superotemporal lens subluxation bilaterally. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "High-frequency, midsystolic click heard at the fifth left intercostal space" -> "Mitral valve prolapse" -> "Connective tissue disorder" -> "Marfan syndrome" -> "Echocardiography indicated" -> 95% CHAIN: "High-arched palate" -> "Marfan syndrome features" -> "Connective tissue disorder" -> "Echocardiography indicated" -> 90% CHAIN: "Abnormally long, slender fingers and toes" -> "Marfan syndrome features" -> "Connective tissue disorder" -> "Echocardiography indicated" -> 90% CHAIN: "Little finger and thumb overlap when clasping wrists" -> "Positive wrist sign for Marfan syndrome" -> "Connective tissue disorder" -> "Echocardiography indicated" -> 90% CHAIN: "Superotemporal lens subluxation on slit lamp examination" -> "Ectopia lentis" -> "Marfan syndrome" -> "Echocardiography indicated" -> 95%
analysis: The clinical presentation of a 4-year-old boy with a high-frequency, midsystolic click, high-arched palate, abnormally long fingers and toes, and lens subluxation is suggestive of Marfan syndrome. The most appropriate next step in management would be to perform an echocardiography to assess for any cardiac abnormalities commonly associated with Marfan syndrome.
